test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 14 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which institute is known as the mother of institutions involved in research on nuclear and accelerator technology?

options.text: Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research
Raja Ramanna Centre for Advanced Technology

solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhabha Atomic Research Centre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) is the premier nuclear research facility of India, headquartered in Trombay, Mumbai.
 
• It was established in 1954 by Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha and is named after him.
 
• BARC is involved in advanced research in nuclear science, engineering, and related areas, including the development of nuclear reactors and fuel cycle technologies.
 
• The institute plays a crucial role in India's nuclear power generation and research programs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Variable Energy Cyclotron Centre (VECC)**

 
 
• VECC is a research and development unit of the Department of Atomic Energy located in Kolkata, India.
 
• It focuses on the study of nuclear physics, particle physics, and accelerator science.
 
• VECC houses the K-130 cyclotron, a major facility for accelerator-based research.
 
 
 
• **Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR)**
 
 
• IGCAR is a premier research institute dedicated to the development of fast reactor technologies.
 
• It is located at Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu, and was established in 1971.
 
• IGCAR plays a significant role in India's nuclear power program, particularly in the Fast Breeder Reactor (FBR) technology.
 
 
 
• **Raja Ramanna Centre for Advanced Technology (RRCAT)**
 
 
• RRCAT, located in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, is a unit of the Department of Atomic Energy.
 
• The center specializes in the development of particle accelerators, lasers, and related technologies.
 
• RRCAT was established in 1984 and named after Dr. Raja Ramanna, a prominent Indian physicist.
